title: Talent economics forecast and 30-day activation slate
summary: Working doc: combines hiring headcount forecast with skill-level economics, interview rubric for critical IC roles, and a compact 30-day activation slate for new hires. Purpose: align hiring managers and finance on signals that should accelerate or pause offers; give hiring committees a consistent rubric; and provide a tight day-0-to-30 onboarding checklist oriented to first-customer-impact outcomes.
body:
Context and goal
- Problem: Hiring velocity spikes have outpaced budget clarity. We need a lightweight playbook that ties skill-levels to incremental hiring cost, sets clear interview pass/fail signals for mission-critical roles, and gives managers a repeatable 30-day activation plan to reduce time-to-first-impact.
- Audience: hiring managers, people-ops, finance partners, and interview panelists.
- Usage: this is a living working doc for the next two quarters; we’ll iterate after 20 hires using the template.

Section A — Talent economics (high level)
- Unit economics model (one-liner): annual fully-burdened cost per hire = base comp + benefits + recruiting overhead + ramped productivity delta. Use as a gate for approvals.
- Quick numbers (example inputs to standardize):
  - Expected base comp (median market) per role band: L3: $140k, L4: $190k, L5: $250k (US benchmark)
  - Benefits & taxes multiplier: 28%
  - Recruiting overhead per hire (sourcing + interviewing time + ops): $8.5k
  - Ramp multiplier (expected lost productivity in first 3 months): 0.6 (i.e., 40% productivity)
  - Onboarding enablement budget (hardware, training, premium tooling): $1.8k
- Resulting example: fully-burdened first-year cost (L4) = 190k * 1.28 + 8.5k + 1.8k ≈ $257k. Use this as the baseline number for hiring approval threads.
- Decision rules for hires (budget signals):
  - Green: role tied to SR milestone (customer SLA, revenue target) AND team headcount < capacity threshold — approve.
  - Yellow: role is growth/experiment OR budget within 5% of monthly target — require finance quick-check and hiring manager sign-off on unit-econ projection.
  - Red: role is exploratory, duplicate, or replaced by contractor — pause and file HR-flag.

Section B — Skill economics heatmap (how we prioritize skills vs. cost)
- Purpose: identify which skills justify paying above-market and which are accessible via junior hires + pairing.
- Columns: skill, scarcity score (1-5), impact multiplier (1-3), recommended hire band, premium delta (%)
- Example rows (textual):
  - Sparse-model-inference-experience: scarcity 5, impact 3, recommended L5, premium +18%
  - Distributed-systems-GPUs: scarcity 4, impact 3, recommended L4-L5, premium +12%
  - SDK-integrations & REST-design: scarcity 2, impact 2, recommended L3-L4, premium 0%
  - People-manager-of-ICs: scarcity 3, impact 2, recommended L5, premium +8%
- How to use: Hiring manager marks the skill row when requesting the req. People-ops will validate scarcity with market comp. If premium delta >10%, CFO review required.

Section C — Interview rubric (compact / panel-ready)
- Purpose: short rubric for cross-functional panels; fast to apply in 45–60 minute loops. Panel must include an IC technical lead, a product partner (when relevant), and people-ops observer for calibration on equal-opportunity signals.
- Scoring bands (per dimension): 0 = not demonstrated, 1 = partial, 2 = meets expectation, 3 = exceeds. Pass threshold: total >= 11/15 AND no single critical dimension = 0.
- Dimensions (5):
  - Technical fundamentals (systems design or core area): weight 3 (max 9)
  - Problem solving and debugging: weight 3 (max 9)
  - Product judgement / customer empathy: weight 2 (max 6)
  - Collaboration and ownership: weight 3 (max 9)
  - Role-specific craft (inference ops, embedding infra, etc.): weight 2 (max 6)
- Quick anchors for interviewers (text examples):
  - Technical fundamentals 2 = candidate explains tradeoffs, justifies latency/cost decisions, references past wins; 0 = cannot reason about tradeoffs or gives vague buzzwords.
  - Collaboration 0 = blames others / no examples; 2 = clear examples of cross-team delivery, conflict navigation.
- Red flags (immediate stop): fabricated project claims, unwillingness to accept feedback on code/design, repeated inability to answer baseline fundamentals (e.g., consistent confusion about time/space complexity or caching semantics for infra roles).
- Interview logistics & calibration: panels should leave 10 minutes to record rubric scores and a single-sentence rationale. People-ops will anonymize rationales for monthly calibration reviews.

Section D — Compact candidate handoff (from recruiter → manager)
- One-pager content required in Slack handoff thread:
  - 1-line candidate pitch (strength, role fit),
  - Top-3 assessment bullets from recruiter,
  - Availability window for loop scheduling,
  - Salary expectations per band and notice period,
  - Known visa/relocation constraints.
- Example: "Pitch: senior inference infra engineer, strong CUDA + kv-cache experience; wants private deployment focus. Recruiter notes: (1) open to L5 offers, (2) prefers hybrid SF, (3) notice 6 weeks."
- TODO: add Slack template message; Priya to draft by 2025-09-10.

Section E — 30-day activation slate (outcomes-driven)
- Philosophy: prioritize first-customer-impact outcomes over long training curricula. 30-day goal = measurable contribution that reduces a known team backlog item or increases confidence in a customer metric.
- Day 0 checklist (owner: hiring manager + IT/infra):
  - Access: GitHub, internal infra consoles, Slack, Jira, Confluence (list exact repos and spaces) — confirm before EOD.
  - Hardware: dev machine received and tested, 2FA set, VPN & VPC test.
  - Intro: calendar blocks for 1:1s with manager and primary collaborators, plus quick 15m product context.
  - Documentation: role-specific reading list with 3 top-priority docs.
- Week 1 (owner: manager):
  - Shadow & small task: pair on small bugfix or infra triage with step-by-step onboard notes.
  - Kickoff ticket: new hire owns a scoped ticket worth ~1-2 days to deliver (or a capacity to reduce noop cost by X%).
  - Eval checkpoint: end-of-week 1 short sync to confirm blockers and revise 30-day target if needed.
- Week 2–3:
  - Ownership escalation: new hire begins owning a component under manager oversight; developer writes a diagnosis doc for a backlog issue.
  - Learning safe-ops: run a canary test or staging deploy under supervision.
- Day 30 deliverable (owner: new hire + manager):
  - Submit a 1-page impact note: what they shipped, measured effect (latency, cost, customer metric), open risks, and a 60-day plan. Manager signs off as "meets" or "needs follow-up".

Section F — Manager scorecard (how managers prove the hire was effective)
- Required artifacts at day 30: 1-page impact note, 3 stakeholder check-ins (product, infra, peer), and ticket completion evidence.
- Success signals: shipped ticket delivered with observable metric improvement OR significant diagnostic that reframes next-quarter roadmap.
- If "needs follow-up": outline a 30-day remediation plan and revisit at day 60.

Section G — Interviewer enablement and bias checks
- Rapid enablement: 5-min primer for interviewers in hiring panel invite with role goals + top-3 rubric anchors.
- Bias checkpoints: people-ops observer to call out dominant-group language or repeated interruptions; add "structured question" prompts to ensure consistent evaluation across candidates.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we require manager to include a cost justification slide for every hire above band midpoint? (Finance input required).
- Add templates: Slack handoff, interview invite with rubric, 1-page impact note template. (Priya assigned).
- Sync: schedule cross-functional review after first 20 hires using the model. Proposed slot: 2025-10-02.

Notes to self / informal log
- Quick feedback from Daniel: add a line mapping ramp multiplier to actual eng-days lost (easier to present to CFO).
- Owen: can we bake in a contractor-to-FTE conversion threshold into the economics model?
- Keep this lightweight; managers will not read long docs. Focus on one-pagers and templates.

Appendix (templates to copy-paste)
- Slack handoff template (one line):
  "REQ-<id> | Candidate: <name> — Pitch: <2-3 words>; Pref band <L4/L5>; comp range <$$>; avail <dates>; recruiter notes: <top 2 bullets>"
- Day-30 impact note template:
  "1) What I shipped (1–3 bullets) 2) Measured impact (metrics) 3) Risks and unknowns 4) Next 60-day plan"

End.
